diagram_math_checks: Objects are exactly S={s,x,y,z,g}, sole goal g, as Counterexample Given; all seven arrows were counted in the final native view. Each arrow is a state transition, not an additional action.
At s, action a has c=1 and P(x|s,a)=1; b has c=1 and P(y|s,b)=1. These are separate action rows, each normalized, matching Given and proof step 2.1.

At x, the unique action has deterministic c=1, with P(x|x)=P(g|x)=1/2; its two arrows sum to one. x is not an absorbing trap: survival after n transitions is 2^-n. This yields f*(x)=2 and the backup f_new(x)=1+f_old(x)/2, matching steps 1.1 and 2.1.
At y and z the unique actions deterministically follow y->z->g, both with c=1 and p=1, giving f*(z)=1 and f*(y)=2. Thus s->y->z->g has cost 3, confirming optimal relevance in step 4.1.

At g, the unique dummy action is the self-loop c=0,p=1. It is absorbing with zero reward, exactly the SSP supplier goal convention. All nonglobal actions have reward -1 and goal reward 0 because r=-c; labels explicitly denote costs, not rewards.

The SSP and RTDP suppliers use undiscounted q_V=r+sum(P V), with no gamma factor. Consequently both initial branches have optimal cost 3 and rewards -3; no discounted value relation has been introduced.
The original claims and five numbered proof steps remain byte-identical and establish the counterexample without using the diagram; the legend expressly states proof independence.
